fixed.title: Death of Queen Victoria
fixed.description: Her Majesty Queen Victoria has passed from this world. The nation is plunged into mourning. All social engagements must be cancelled for the season.
fixed.flavourText: A black-edged memorandum circulates through every department: 'It is desired that all officers of the Civil Service observe the appropriate period of Court Mourning.'

choices.text: Observe the full mourning period with solemn propriety.
choices.flavorResponse: Your discretion is noted by senior colleagues. A small mark of approval is entered against your name.

choices.text: Attend a private gala — surely one small gathering cannot matter.
choices.flavorResponse: Word reaches the Permanent Secretary's office. You are regarded as a man of questionable taste.

fixed.title: Boer War: Peace of Vereeniging
fixed.description: The protracted conflict in South Africa has finally ended. Departments attached to the War Office are overwhelmed with administrative work.
fixed.flavourText: The corridors of Whitehall hum with a renewed sense of imperial purpose. Extra clerks are being drafted in.

choices.text: Volunteer for the special War Office administrative detail.
choices.flavorResponse: Your dedication is rewarded with a commendation from the War Office. Your energy reserves are considerably depleted, however.

choices.text: Continue your ordinary duties. The matter does not concern your department.
choices.flavorResponse: Business proceeds as usual in your corner of Whitehall.

fixed.title: Liberal Party Landslide
fixed.description: The Liberals have swept into power with a great majority. The ministerial landscape shifts dramatically; your Tory patrons find themselves on the opposition benches.
fixed.flavourText: The new Permanent Secretary — a man of decidedly Radical inclinations — surveys his department with fresh eyes.

choices.text: Discreetly cultivate relations with the new Liberal ministerial set.
choices.flavorResponse: You navigate the transition with pragmatic skill. Several old Tory connections quietly note your flexibility.

choices.text: Maintain the strict neutrality expected of a permanent official.
choices.flavorResponse: Your impartiality is remarked upon. You are the very model of a Northcote-Trevelyan official.

choices.text: Privately maintain your Tory connections, hoping for a swift return to power.
choices.flavorResponse: Your partisan inclinations do not go unnoticed. The new set regards you with suspicion.

fixed.title: Old Age Pensions Act
fixed.description: Parliament has passed the Old Age Pensions Act. The Treasury and Local Government Board are inundated with administrative work of unprecedented scale.
fixed.flavourText: Mountains of forms requiring verification arrive daily. The indexing room resembles a paper manufactory.

choices.text: Take charge of organising the pensions administration in your sub-department.
choices.flavorResponse: Your capacity for organisation under pressure earns you the quiet respect of your superiors.

choices.text: Delegate the bulk of the work to junior clerks while you manage at a higher level.
choices.flavorResponse: A competent approach, if not a heroic one. The junior clerks grumble, but the work gets done.

fixed.title: The Parliament Act Crisis
fixed.description: A constitutional crisis engulfs Westminster. The Lords have challenged the Commons; record-keeping and departmental correspondence are under intense scrutiny.
fixed.flavourText: Every minute and memorandum may be called as evidence before a Select Committee. Fastidiousness is now a survival skill.

choices.text: Devote extra energy to ensuring all departmental records are immaculate.
choices.flavorResponse: Your files are models of administrative propriety. Should any inquiry come, your department will be found blameless.

choices.text: Quietly destroy several embarrassing internal memoranda.
choices.flavorResponse: The destruction is noticed by a junior clerk. A shadow falls over your name.

fixed.title: Outbreak of the Great War
fixed.description: War has been declared. All departmental leave is suspended. The energy cost of all administrative work is doubled for the foreseeable future.
fixed.flavourText: 'Business as usual' proclaimed the Chancellor, but there is nothing usual about the feverish activity now overtaking Whitehall.

choices.text: Throw yourself into the war effort with full commitment.
choices.flavorResponse: Your dedication to King and Country is noted. The extra burden, however, taxes you considerably.

choices.text: Maintain steady, diligent service without overextension.
choices.flavorResponse: You soldier on as Whitehall adapts to the new reality.

fixed.title: Sex Disqualification (Removal) Act
fixed.description: Women are now eligible to compete for Class I posts in the Civil Service. The old 'club' atmosphere of the Higher Division begins to shift.
fixed.flavourText: Several senior officials are observed to be conspicuously uncomfortable at the sight of the new lady clerks presenting their examination credentials.

choices.text: Welcome the new colleagues as a modernising and capable addition to the service.
choices.flavorResponse: You are regarded as a man of progressive sensibility. Certain reactionary colleagues view you with suspicion.

choices.text: Make no comment but quietly ensure the traditional ways are maintained in your section.
choices.flavorResponse: Your obstructionism is eventually noticed. A note is appended to your conduct file.

choices.text: Treat the matter as you would any other administrative change: with professional neutrality.
choices.flavorResponse: An appropriately bureaucratic response. The matter proceeds without incident in your section.

procedural.title: The Disgruntled Clerk
procedural.description: A subordinate has discovered an arithmetic error in one of your ledger entries from last quarter. He lingers at the door of your office with a meaningful expression.
procedural.flavourText: Dobson clears his throat. 'I wonder, sir, if you might cast an eye over these figures. I believe there may be a... discrepancy.'

choices.text: Press a sovereign into his palm and suggest the ledger entry was a fair copy of an earlier error.
choices.flavorResponse: Dobson pockets the coin with admirable discretion. The ledger entry is quietly corrected.

choices.text: Dismiss him with a look of bland incomprehension. The error was surely trivial.
choices.flavorResponse: Dobson withdraws, unconvinced. You notice him whispering with the other junior clerks.

choices.text: Acknowledge the error, thank him formally, and submit a corrected return.
choices.flavorResponse: A minor embarrassment, but your transparency is appreciated. Dobson leaves looking mildly surprised.

choices.text: Arrange a small promotion for Dobson to the copying room — a most convenient posting.
choices.flavorResponse: Dobson departs to his new post with suspicious alacrity. The matter is closed, at a price.

procedural.title: The Anonymous Tip
procedural.description: A document from your desk has been leaked to The Times. The morning edition carries a leading article on internal Treasury deliberations.
procedural.flavourText: The Permanent Secretary enters your room with a face of grey stone and a copy of The Times folded to the relevant page.

choices.text: Initiate a discreet internal investigation to identify the source of the leak.
choices.flavorResponse: You narrow it down to two suspects but cannot act without firm evidence. The atmosphere in the room becomes frosty.

choices.text: Accept full responsibility in the interests of departmental loyalty.
choices.flavorResponse: An act of considerable sacrifice. Your superiors are grateful. Your record, however, bears a permanent mark.

choices.text: Suggest, with suitable regret, that the fault likely lies with the junior division.
choices.flavorResponse: The junior clerks are furious. Several senior colleagues regard your manoeuvre with distaste.

procedural.title: The Etiquette Gaffe
procedural.description: You have arrived at a formal dinner wearing a black tie. The occasion demands a white tie. The hostess — wife of the Permanent Secretary — has noticed.
procedural.flavourText: Lady Holsworth's glance travels from your neckwear to your face with an expression of refined discomfort.

choices.text: Apologise to the hostess immediately and make a discreet, early departure.
choices.flavorResponse: Your swift departure limits the damage. The incident is noted but not dwelt upon.

choices.text: Proceed as though nothing is amiss. A confident man sets his own rules.
choices.flavorResponse: The gamble fails utterly. Your name is mentioned with a delicate shudder in three drawing rooms by Thursday.

choices.text: Offer a charming, self-deprecating explanation — an urgent despatch detained you.
choices.flavorResponse: Lady Holsworth is partially appeased. Your wit saves the evening, if not your reputation entirely.

procedural.title: The 'Chumocracy' Opportunity
procedural.description: A donor to the ruling party has made contact through an intermediary. He requires a favourable interpretation of certain trade regulations in exchange for 'consideration'.
procedural.flavourText: A note, unsigned, arrives at your private address: 'The matter of the Manchester cotton contracts might be viewed with flexibility. Our friend in the City is most appreciative of flexible minds.'

choices.text: Accept the arrangement. The regulations are ambiguous; one's interpretation is one's own.
choices.flavorResponse: The funds arrive through a solicitor's account. The trade contract is awarded. You feel the greasy pole beneath your feet.

choices.text: Report the approach to the Permanent Secretary.
choices.flavorResponse: The Permanent Secretary commends your integrity. An inquiry is quietly shelved. Several colleagues look at you oddly.

choices.text: Ignore the note. Burn it, and say nothing.
choices.flavorResponse: Nothing further transpires. You sleep moderately well.

procedural.title: A Season of Ill Health
procedural.description: The relentless pace of the office and the damp of a London winter have caught up with you. Your doctor recommends rest.
procedural.flavourText: Dr Pemberton sets down his stethoscope with a grave expression. 'The strain of modern administrative life, I'm afraid. You must take the waters at Bath.'

choices.text: Take a fortnight's leave and recover your constitution at Bath.
choices.flavorResponse: You return refreshed and considerably improved. The work, alas, has piled up in your absence.

choices.text: Press on regardless. The service does not pause for sentiment.
choices.flavorResponse: You persist, but at a considerable cost to your constitution and your temper.

procedural.title: The Tobacco Box
procedural.description: A building contractor seeking a government supply contract approaches you in the Travellers Club. He places a handsome tobacco box on the table between you with a meaningful smile.
procedural.flavourText: 'For a man of discernment,' he says, with a wink that would shame a pantomime villain.

choices.text: Accept the box with a nod. The tobacco within is most certainly not tobacco.
choices.flavorResponse: You pocket the screwed-up notes with a steady hand. The contractor departs satisfied.

choices.text: Decline with a polite fiction about preferring a particular brand.
choices.flavorResponse: The contractor smiles thinly and departs. You order another glass of claret.

procedural.title: Intrigue at the Country House
procedural.description: You are invited to a weekend at a Buckinghamshire estate. Another guest — a rising ministerial aide — is clearly attempting to cultivate your influence.
procedural.flavourText: Over billiards, Harrington-Smythe leans close: 'I say, old man, I wonder if a word from you to Under-Secretary Carrington might smooth a particular matter...'

choices.text: Agree to put in a discreet word. Such arrangements are the cement of the service.
choices.flavorResponse: The favour is done. Harrington-Smythe is effusively grateful. You have accumulated a useful obligation.

choices.text: Express warm interest but commit to nothing. The weekend proceeds pleasantly.
choices.flavorResponse: A diplomatic response. Harrington-Smythe is mildly disappointed but does not press the matter.

choices.text: Decline with polite firmness. The impartiality of the service must be maintained.
choices.flavorResponse: Your principled stance earns a degree of respect. Harrington-Smythe calls you a prig under his breath.

procedural.title: Results of the Competitive Examination
procedural.description: The Civil Service Commission has published the results of the competitive examination. Your placement in the list will determine your initial standing.
procedural.flavourText: The list is posted in the entrance hall. Your fingers trace the columns of names until they find your own.

choices.text: You have placed in the first division of the examination.
choices.flavorResponse: Congratulations circulate through the department. 'A man of real ability,' the Principal Clerk remarks.
